But in about three months this swelling goes down and looks super natural.

Oh, no, but that is already included in the package.

words.gram: spoken confirmation tag from não é

lines.trans: Do you remember what her dark circles were like?
Look, it already brightened up nicely, right now it is a bit swollen.
But in about three months this swelling goes down and looks super natural.
Sorry, you could not have done this without our authorization.
Oh, no, but that is already included in the package.
All funeral homes offer this service now.
Just look at this foundation. It does not transfer, see? Look, bone dry.
No, you are going to have to take this off our mother right now.
Bye!

meanings.note: Affirmative reply; paired with senhor here for mock-obedient office humour.

examples.trans: Yes, sir.
Yes, we are ready.

meanings.note: Introduces a contrast. The informal thanks softens the refusal; it does not accept the invitation.

examples.trans: I’m not going, but thanks.
It’s a meeting, but I’m not going.

meanings.note: Used here for being present at an event. Vou estar keeps estar in the infinitive after the finite form vou.

examples.trans: I’m not going to be at that meeting.
Are you going to be at that meeting?

meanings.note: Absolute superlative (-íssimo) of belo.

examples.trans: Yes, but she looks gorgeous, right?
The work turned out stunning.

meanings.note: Ubiquitous spoken contraction of não é used to invite agreement.

examples.text: Isso aqui é um gráfico, né?
examples.trans: This here is a chart, right?
It's Monday, right?

meanings.note: A person being addressed, with third-person verb agreement: você vai, vocês vão. Vai and vão are forms of ir, not forms of the pronoun. Common in Brazil; not a rule that every Brazilian region uses the same address system.

examples.trans: Are you going to the meeting?
Are you in finance?

meanings.note: Used without a preposition before a clause: Você lembra como era?

examples.text: Você lembra como era a olheira dela?
examples.trans: Do you remember what her dark circles were like?
I remember that very well.

meanings.note: Often reinforced with é que in questions (como é que foi?).

examples.text: Como é que foi a cirurgia?
examples.trans: How did the surgery go?

examples.text: Como é que tá meu marido?
examples.trans: How is my husband doing?

meanings.note: Used for identifying a type of meeting or the department a person belongs to. The present forms sou and é are irregular.

examples.trans: I’m in finance.
It’s a marketing meeting.

meanings.note: All-purpose connector, relative link, question opener, and comparative word after mais or melhor.

examples.text: Eu acho que ele já foi.
examples.trans: I think that he already left.
What is this, man?

meanings.note: Definite article agreeing in gender and number with its noun; also common before given names in casual Brazilian speech.

examples.trans: What is your job title?
Look at the young woman over there.

meanings.note: Dark or sunken area under the eyes.

examples.text: Você lembra como era a olheira dela?
examples.trans: Do you remember what her dark circles were like?
I have big dark circles today.

meanings.note: Contraction of de + ela, placed after the noun in Brazil to mean her.

examples.trans: She got ahead on her work.
I need her help.

meanings.note: Used as a quick imperative olha! (look!) and in future subjunctive se vocês olharem (if you look).

examples.trans: Look inside there.

examples.text: Se vocês olharem bem, tem números.
examples.trans: If you look closely, there are numbers.

meanings.note: Doubled as já, já, it means 'very soon / any minute now'.

examples.trans: Your husband is already doing great.
I have already been in that situation.

meanings.note: Versatile core verb; dando falsa esperança means giving false hope.

examples.text: Ele está dando falsa esperança pra nós.
examples.trans: He is giving us false hope.
Give it a rest!

meanings.note: Indefinite article; plural uns and umas mean some or a few in everyday Brazilian Portuguese.

examples.trans: Shall we have a little coffee?
There are some good numbers.

meanings.note: Before an action noun in dar uma bela rejuvenescida, means 'a really nice/proper'.

examples.trans: It gives a lovely rejuvenation, right?
It already brightened up nicely.

meanings.note: In dar uma clareada, colloquial Brazilian action noun for brightening up.

examples.trans: It has already brightened up nicely.

examples.text: O creme deu uma clareada na pele.
examples.trans: The cream brightened the skin a bit.

meanings.note: Marks the current moment resulting from an earlier action.

examples.trans: Now she is in a meeting.

examples.text: Agora tenho que resolver umas coisinhas.
examples.trans: Right now I have to sort out a few little things.

meanings.note: Diminutive of inchado (swollen), used to downplay post-procedure swelling.

examples.text: Agora tá inchadinho, mas já desincha.
examples.trans: Right now it is a bit swollen, but the swelling will go down.
Her face got a bit puffy.

meanings.note: Neutral demonstrative pronoun pointing to what was just said or done.

examples.trans: What is this, man?
That slows everyone else down.

meanings.note: Points to the speaker's location or reinforces demonstratives like isso aqui and esse slide aqui.

examples.text: Ela veio aqui olhar um extintor.
examples.trans: She came here to check an extinguisher.
This here is a chart.

meanings.note: Contraction of de + aqui.

examples.text: A dor pega daqui até o pescoço.
examples.trans: The pain goes from here up to my neck.
We are close to here.

meanings.note: Links verbs like faltar to an event or destination.

examples.trans: She missed a meeting.
In an hour.

meanings.note: Invariable cardinal number.

examples.text: Ela tá três anos aqui procurando.
examples.trans: She has been here for three years looking.
I have three things to sort out.

meanings.note: Calendar month; plural meses drops the circumflex.

examples.trans: I will deposit up to six months.

examples.text: Falta um mês para a viagem.
examples.trans: There is one month left until the trip.

meanings.note: Formed with prefix des- + inchar (to swell).

examples.text: Daqui a três meses já desincha.
examples.trans: In three months the swelling goes down.
Her face has already lost the swelling.

meanings.note: Coordinating conjunction pronounced [i] in natural Brazilian speech.

examples.text: Ela faltou e adiantou o trabalho.
examples.trans: She missed it and got ahead on her work.
There are good and bad numbers.

meanings.note: Expresses staying in a place or state (ficar sentado, fica no celular).

examples.trans: You're going to stay seated.

examples.text: Ela fica no celular o dia todo.
examples.trans: She stays on her phone all day.

meanings.note: Colloquial intensifier before adjectives in Brazilian Portuguese.

examples.trans: It looks super natural.
She is super friendly.

meanings.note: Looking natural or unforced.

examples.trans: It looks super natural.
The result is very natural.

meanings.note: Used standalone in Brazilian speech as the everyday informal sorry.

examples.trans: Sorry, folks.
Sorry for the delay!

meanings.note: A negative answer or a negation in a sentence. A final repeated não can reinforce a conversational refusal in Brazil.

examples.trans: No, I’m not going.
Aren’t you going?

poder.gloss: can; may; to be able to

meanings.en: can; may; to be able to
meanings.note: Core modal verb followed by an infinitive.

examples.text: O senhor pode ser meu fiador?
examples.trans: Can you be my guarantor, sir?
I cannot right now.

meanings.note: Expresses possession, obligation in ter que + infinitive, and impersonal existence (tem alguns números, there are some numbers).

examples.text: Eu tenho que entrar lá dentro.
examples.trans: I have to go inside there.
There are some good numbers.

meanings.note: Irregular past eu fiz (I made/did); não tem o que fazer means having nothing to do.

examples.text: Ela não tem o que fazer agora.
examples.trans: She has nothing to do now.

examples.text: Esse slide aqui eu fiz ontem.
examples.trans: This slide here I made yesterday.

meanings.note: Indicates lack or absence.

examples.trans: I am missing both legs.
I drink coffee without sugar.

meanings.note: First-person plural possessive agreeing in gender and number with the noun.

examples.text: Ela está com a nossa equipe.
examples.trans: She is with our team.
Our work ran late.

meanings.note: Official or family permission.

examples.text: Você fez isso sem a nossa autorização.
examples.trans: You did this without our authorization.
I need your authorization.

meanings.note: Expresses sudden realization or understanding.

examples.text: Ah, ele veio fazer implante capilar?
examples.trans: Oh, he came to get a hair implant?
Oh, now I get it!

meanings.note: Short participle of incluir used with estar: tá incluso no pacote.

examples.text: Isso já tá incluso no pacote.
examples.trans: That is already included in the package.
Coffee is included.

meanings.note: Usually contracts with definite articles to no, na, nos, nas.

examples.trans: He is in the meeting.
She stays on her phone.

meanings.note: A service bundle or physical parcel.

examples.text: Isso já tá incluso no pacote.
examples.trans: That is already included in the package.
We booked the full package.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender and number; before an adjective (todo travado) means completely.

examples.text: A culpa toda disso foi dele.
examples.trans: All the blame for this was his.
I am all locked up in my neck.

meanings.note: Business that arranges wakes and burials.

examples.text: Todas as funerárias estão com esse serviço.
examples.trans: All funeral homes offer this service.
The funeral home is downtown.

meanings.note: Marks accompaniment or an added ingredient such as sweetener.

examples.trans: I want coffee with sweetener.

examples.text: Ela está com a nossa equipe.
examples.trans: She is with our team.

meanings.note: Demonstrative determiner; in spoken Brazilian Portuguese esse commonly covers both this near me and that just mentioned.

examples.text: Esse slide aqui eu fiz ontem.
examples.trans: This slide here I made yesterday.

examples.text: Vou ficar sentado esse tempo inteiro.
examples.trans: I'm going to stay seated that whole time.

meanings.note: Professional service or work offered to clients.

examples.trans: All of them have this service.
The service was fast.

meanings.note: Limits a statement (eu só quero) or forms só que (except that / the catch is).

examples.text: Eu só quero saber o motivo.
examples.trans: I just want to know the reason.

examples.text: Só que agora ela precisa de ajuda.
examples.trans: Except now she needs help.

meanings.note: Core foundation or support of a system.

examples.text: O verde e amarelo é nossa base.
examples.trans: The green and yellow is our foundation.

examples.text: Essa é a base do projeto.
examples.trans: This is the foundation of the project.

meanings.note: In makeup tutorials, não transfere means the foundation does not rub off onto clothes or fingers.

examples.text: Olha só essa base, não transfere.
examples.trans: Just look at this foundation, it does not transfer.
He transferred the money.

meanings.note: Gerund vendo pairs with estar (tá vendo, do you see), and tem que ver means we have to look into it.

examples.text: Você tá vendo aquela moça ali?
examples.trans: Do you see that young woman over there?
We need to look into that later.

meanings.note: Diminutive of seco (dry), used in beauty tutorials for a non-oily matte finish.

examples.trans: Look, it stays nice and dry.
The skin stays nice and matte.

meanings.note: Vou + infinitive can express a future intention: vou estar means I am going to be. Você takes the third-person vai.

examples.trans: I’m going to the meeting.
Aren’t you going?

meanings.note: Everyday verb for removing or taking something out.

examples.trans: We took it out during surgery.

examples.text: Você tira o botão de baixo.
examples.trans: You take the button from the bottom.

meanings.note: Links a meeting with its subject. Do is de + the masculine article o; sou do financeiro identifies membership in the finance department.

examples.trans: It’s a marketing meeting.
I’m in finance.

meanings.note: Female parent; plural mães.

examples.text: Meu pai e minha mãe me bloquearam.
examples.trans: My dad and my mom blocked me.

examples.text: Vou voltar pra casa da minha mãe.
examples.trans: I am going to go back to my mother's house.

meanings.note: Everyday friendly farewell across Brazil, borrowed long ago from Italian ciao.

examples.trans: Bye, see you tomorrow!
Bye, folks!
